title: Distinct synaptic plasticity rules operate across dendritic compartments in vivo during learning
goal: Reproduce the original compartment-specific relationships of local synaptic coactivity and input–somatic coincidence to subsequent spine strengthening, together with the source Kir/control effects on structural plasticity during motor learning. Preserve each named result's original compartment, training stage, spine/dendrite/mouse populations and the measurement, spatial, timing, suppression, homeostasis and distance controls needed for its interpretation. Retain the four-correlation reconstruction as partial evidence and the full18 released-source programme as a separately scoped source component; neither defines complete primary success by itself. Separate behavioral learning trajectories do not establish a Kir-versus-control learning effect.

success_criteria: Assess reproduction and improvement independently under reproduction.v2.json and improvement.v1.json; do not combine their scores.
